questions.question: Compare evolutionary and cultural explanations of non-verbal behaviour.

points.text: Evolutionary: NVC evolved for survival (e.g. expressions signal intent, eye contact signals threat). Supported by universality and blind individuals showing expressions. Cultural: NVC is learned through socialisation. Supported by cultural differences in display rules, gestures, and proxemics. Both contribute - NVC has an innate basis modified by cultural learning.

questions.question: Describe Yuki's study on cultural differences in interpreting facial expressions and evaluate its methodology.

points.text: Yuki (2007): American and Japanese participants judged emotions from eyes vs mouths. Americans relied more on mouths (expressive, open culture); Japanese relied more on eyes (subtle cues matter in collectivist culture). Evaluation: controlled methodology, but used static images rather than real interaction; samples were university students (limited generalisability); demonstrates cultural shaping

questions.question: Discuss whether non-verbal behaviour is primarily innate or learned.

points.text: Innate evidence: universal facial expressions (Ekman); blind individuals show same expressions; infants express emotions without learning. Learned evidence: display rules vary; gestures differ by culture; Yuki's study shows interpretation is cultural.
